e.etymology: A short form of Antonia for girls and, in much of Europe, of Anton and Antonio for boys. All go back to the Roman family name Antonius, whose meaning is unknown.
namesakes: Toni Morrison (Nobel Prize-winning author of Beloved)
Toni Braxton (R&B singer of Un-Break My Heart)
Toni Collette (actress in The Sixth Sense and Hereditary)

e.etymology: The German and Dutch spelling of Stephen, from Greek stephanos, a crown or wreath. Saint Stephen is the first Christian martyr in the Book of Acts.
An African American coinage of the late 20th century that joins the Ja- prefix of Jamal and Jamar to Marion or the -ion ending.

e.meaning: bailiff, or dweller by the castle wall
e.etymology: A spelling of Bailey, an English surname for a bailiff or steward, or for someone who lived by a bailey, the outer wall of a castle.
From a surname with several sources, most often German Keller, cellar or storehouse, for a cellar master. It joined other -er surname names such as Sawyer and Miller.

assoc.t: Helen Keller, deaf-blind author and activist

e.etymology: A pet form of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious, with the -ie ending. It has long been given as a full name to both boys and girls, especially in the American South.
namesakes: Johnnie Cochran (defense attorney in the O.J. Simpson trial)

e.etymology: A spelling of Hailey or Hayley, an English surname from a place name, Old English heg, hay, and leah, clearing. Eminem's daughter Hailie, named in his songs, made this spelling familiar in the early 2000s.

assoc.t: Hailie Jade, Eminem's daughter, named in his songs

e.meaning: army man (as Armand); also Hebrew for palace
e.etymology: A name with more than one source: a variant of Armand, the French form of the Germanic name Herman, army man, and the Hebrew word armon, palace or castle.

e.meaning: an Irish form of Mary; in Latin, dark or Moorish
e.etymology: Two names share the spelling: an anglicized form of Irish Máire, Mary, and the feminine of Latin Maurus, a Moor or dark-skinned person, borne by early saints.
namesakes: Maura Tierney (actress of ER and NewsRadio)

e.etymology: A Latin American short form of Elizabeth, in the same family as Lizbeth and Lisette. Elizabeth comes from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath.
From avril, the French word for April, taken up as an English given name in the 20th century. In the US it rose in the 2000s with singer Avril Lavigne.
namesakes: Avril Lavigne (pop-punk singer of Complicated and Sk8er Boi)

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that echoes azure, the word for sky blue, and Zuri, a Swahili name meaning beautiful. It has no settled meaning of its own.
Coined by American fantasy author Brandon Sanderson for Kaladin Stormblessed, the soldier hero of The Stormlight Archive, which began with The Way of Kings in 2010.
namesakes: Kaladin Stormblessed (hero of Brandon Sanderson's Stormlight Archive)

assoc.t: hero of Brandon Sanderson's Stormlight Archive novels

e.etymology: A spelling of Tanya, the Russian pet form of Tatiana, which comes from the Roman family name Tatius. This spelling is the usual one in Spanish, Portuguese and Italian.
A spelling of Helen, from Greek Helene, probably related to a word for a torch or bright light. In Greek myth Hellen, with two Ls, is also the male ancestor of the Hellenes, the Greeks.
An American coinage, a fanciful spelling of Louanna (Lou plus Anna). The play and film Bird of Paradise gave the name to a Hawaiian princess, and it was later linked to Hawaiian luana, leisure.
A variant of Noelle, the feminine of French Noël, Christmas, from Latin natalis dies, day of birth. It is often chosen for girls born near Christmas.
From an English surname and place name, Arley, from Old English earn, eagle, and leah, wood or clearing. Its recent rise follows Arlo, Harley and Marley.

From Tibetan bstan 'dzin, one who holds the teachings, that is, the Buddhist dharma. It is part of the 14th Dalai Lama's name, Tenzin Gyatso, and many Tibetan boys and girls are named Tenzin in his honor.
namesakes: Tenzin (Aang's airbender son in The Legend of Korra)

assoc.t: Aang's airbender son in The Legend of Korra

e.etymology: In South India, from Sanskrit sahana, patience or forbearance, also the name of a raga in Carnatic music. In Bengali, Sahana is a form of Shahana, from a Persian word for royal.
A respelling of Lincoln made familiar by the rock band Linkin Park. Lincoln is an English city name from Celtic lindo, pool, and Latin colonia, settlement.
A feminine form of Charles coined in the 19th century with the -ene ending of Marlene and Helene. Charles comes from a Germanic word for a free man.
namesakes: Princess Charlene of Monaco (former Olympic swimmer)

e.etymology: In Croatian, Serbian, Czech and Bulgarian use, the feminine of Ivo, a short form of Ivan (John) that is also linked to a Germanic word for yew. It was well used in the US around 1900.
A spelling of Brianna, the feminine of Brian, an Irish name probably from a Celtic word for high or noble. Brianna spread in the US from the 1970s.
A coinage from the endearment darling with the -ene ending of Charlene and Marlene, in use since the late 19th century and most popular in mid-century America.
namesakes: Darlene Love (singer of Christmas (Baby Please Come Home))
Darlene Conner (sardonic daughter on Roseanne and The Conners)

e.etymology: From an English surname and place name, Old English aewell, river source, and tun, settlement.
namesakes: Alton Brown (Food Network host of Good Eats)

assoc.t: Alton, Illinois, river city near St. Louis

e.etymology: A spelling of Heidi favored in Latin America. Heidi is the Swiss German pet form of Adelheid (Adelaide), noble kind, made famous by the 1880 children's novel Heidi.

In Chinese, Jia can be written with characters such as 佳, fine or beautiful, and 嘉, excellent or auspicious. In India, Jia or Jiya means heart or sweetheart. Some American parents also use it as a spelling of Gia.
A pet form of Hadley and Hadassah, and a sound-alike of Hattie and Addie. It rose in the 2010s after the character Haddie Braverman on the TV drama Parenthood.

assoc.t: Haddie Braverman, teen daughter on NBC's Parenthood

e.etymology: From the Irish surname Ó Ruadhagáin, descendant of Ruadhagán, a pet form of ruadh, red or red-haired.
A respelling of Crystal, the English word for clear quartz, from Greek krystallos, ice. K spellings rose in the 1980s alongside Krystle Carrington of the TV drama Dynasty.

assoc.t: Krystal, Southern fast-food chain known for small burgers

e.etymology: The Italian form of Joseph, from Hebrew Yosef, he will add, by way of Greek and Latin.
namesakes: Giuseppe Verdi (composer of La Traviata and Aida)
Giuseppe Garibaldi (general who helped unify Italy)
